# Backend Profile Fetch Implementation
## What Was Implemented
Your `FlutterDashboardActivity` now **fetches user profile data from the backend** when the dashboard is opened.
## Flow Diagram
``` User Logs In ↓ Login provides: email, userId, token (Intent extras) ↓ FlutterDashboardActivity.onCreate() ↓ setupMethodChannels() ↓ 1. Send basic session data to Flutter (email, userId, token) ↓ 2. fetchUserProfile(token, channel) ← NEW! ↓ Backend API Call: GET /api/v1/me (with JWT token) ↓ Backend returns full profile: - email - cognitoSub - displayName - fullName - mfaEnabled - role ↓ 3. Send full profile data to Flutter via MethodChannel ```
## Code Changes
### 1. FlutterDashboardActivity.kt
Added `fetchUserProfile()` method that: - Calls the backend API endpoint `/api/v1/me` - Uses the JWT token for authentication (automatically added by RetrofitClient) - Parses the response and extracts profile data - Sends the full profile to Flutter via MethodChannel
```kotlin private fun fetchUserProfile(token: String, channel: MethodChannel) { lifecycleScope.launch { try { val apiService = RetrofitClient.getApiService() val response = apiService.getUserProfile()
if (response.isSuccessful && response.body() != null) { val profile = response.body()!!
// Send full profile to Flutter val fullUserSession = mapOf( "email" to profile["email"], "userId" to profile["cognitoSub"], "displayName" to profile["displayName"], "fullName" to profile["fullName"], "mfaEnabled" to profile["mfaEnabled"], "role" to profile["role"], ... )
channel.invokeMethod("updateUserSession", fullUserSession) } } catch (e: Exception) { Timber.e(e, "Error fetching user profile") } } } ```
### 2. ApiService.kt
Added the endpoint definition:
```kotlin @GET("api/v1/me") suspend fun getUserProfile(): Response<Map<String, Any>> ```
## Backend API Endpoint
Your Spring Boot controller at `/api/v1/me`:
```java @GetMapping public ResponseEntity<UserProfileDTO> getCurrentUser( @AuthenticationPrincipal Jwt jwt, HttpServletRequest request) {
String cognitoSub = jwt.getClaimAsString("sub"); String email = jwt.getClaimAsString("email");
// Create or update user in DB userService.createOrUpdateUserFromJwt(jwt);
// Get the user profile UserProfileDTO profile = userService.getCurrentUser(cognitoSub);
return ResponseEntity.ok(profile); } ```
## What Happens Now
### Step 1: Initial Session (Fast) When FlutterDashboardActivity opens: - Sends basic session data immediately (email, userId, token) - Flutter dashboard can display user info right away
### Step 2: Full Profile Fetch (Async) In the background: - Calls backend API `/api/v1/me` - Retrieves full profile including: - Display name - Full name - MFA status - User role - Any other fields in UserProfileDTO
### Step 3: Update Flutter - Sends updated profile data to Flutter - Flutter can update UI with additional info
## Benefits
✅ **Fast Initial Load**: User sees dashboard immediately with basic info ✅ **Complete Profile**: Full profile data fetched from backend ✅ **Always Up-to-Date**: Gets latest data from database on every dashboard open ✅ **Error Handling**: Falls back to basic session data if backend fails ✅ **Audit Logging**: Backend logs profile fetch as "PROFILE_FETCH" event
## Testing
### Test 1: Successful Profile Fetch 1. Login to the app 2. Navigate to Flutter Dashboard 3. Check Logcat for: ``` Fetching user profile from backend... Full user profile sent to Flutter: user@example.com ``` 4. Flutter should receive full profile with displayName, role, etc.
### Test 2: Backend Error Handling 1. Disconnect network or stop backend 2. Navigate to Flutter Dashboard 3. Check Logcat for: ``` Error fetching user profile from backend: ... ``` 4. Flutter still works with basic session data (email, userId)
### Test 3: View Profile Page 1. Open Flutter Dashboard 2. Click "View Profile" action card 3. Should display all profile fields fetched from backend
## Profile Data Structure
The backend returns (based on your UserProfileDTO):
```json { "cognitoSub": "uuid-string", "email": "user@example.com", "displayName": "John Doe", "fullName": "John Michael Doe", "mfaEnabled": false, "role": "USER", "createdAt": "2025-12-11T10:00:00", "updatedAt": "2025-12-11T15:30:00" } ```
Flutter receives this via MethodChannel as:
```dart { 'email': 'user@example.com', 'userId': 'uuid-string', 'accessToken': 'jwt-token', 'displayName': 'John Doe', 'fullName': 'John Michael Doe', 'mfaEnabled': false, 'role': 'USER', 'fcmToken': 'fcm-token' } ```
## Troubleshooting
### Issue: 401 Unauthorized **Cause**: JWT token not being sent or expired **Solution**: Check RetrofitClient is adding Authorization header
### Issue: 500 Internal Server Error **Cause**: Backend user not found or database error **Solution**: - Check backend logs - Verify `userService.createOrUpdateUserFromJwt(jwt)` works - Ensure user exists in database
### Issue: Network timeout **Cause**: Backend unreachable **Solution**: - Verify backend is running - Check base URL in RetrofitClient - Ensure device/emulator can reach backend
## Next Steps
You can extend this to: 1. **Cache profile data** locally to reduce API calls 2. **Update profile** via PATCH /api/v1/me 3. **Toggle MFA** via POST /api/v1/me/mfa/toggle 4. **Refresh profile** when user returns to dashboard 5. **Show more profile fields** in ProfilePage widget
## Files Modified
1. ✅ `app/src/main/java/com/example/androidapp/ui/FlutterDashboardActivity.kt` - Added `fetchUserProfile()` method - Calls backend on dashboard open
2. ✅ `app/src/main/java/com/example/androidapp/data/remote/api/ApiService.kt` - Added `getUserProfile()` endpoint
3. ✅ `flutter_module/lib/features/profile/presentation/pages/profile_page.dart` - Already handles profile data from MethodChannel - Displays all received fields
All code compiles successfully with no errors!

# CRITICAL BUG FIXED - Bluetooth Scan Not Working
## The Problem
Your Bluetooth scan was **completely failing silently**. Looking at your logs:
``` 21:46:11.161 BluetoothHandler: startScanning called, launching coroutine with duration=10000 21:46:11.163 BluetoothHandler: Returning success to Flutter immediately ```
After that - **NOTHING!** No logs from inside the coroutine, no scan activity, nothing.
## Root Cause - INDENTATION BUG
There was a **critical indentation error** in `BluetoothHandler.kt` line 251:
### BEFORE (BROKEN): ```kotlin withTimeoutOrNull(timeoutMs) { android.util.Log.d("BluetoothHandler", "Inside withTimeoutOrNull, calling repository.startScan") repository.startScan(duration) // ❌ WRONG INDENTATION - OUTSIDE THE BLOCK! .catch { e -> ```
The `repository.startScan(duration)` call was **outside** the `withTimeoutOrNull` block due to incorrect indentation. This caused: 1. The Kotlin compiler to misinterpret the code structure 2. The coroutine to fail to launch properly 3. Silent failure with no error logs
### AFTER (FIXED): ```kotlin withTimeoutOrNull(timeoutMs) { android.util.Log.d("BluetoothHandler", "Inside withTimeoutOrNull, calling repository.startScan") repository.startScan(duration) // ✅ CORRECT - INSIDE THE BLOCK! .catch { e -> ```
Now `repository.startScan(duration)` is **properly inside** the `withTimeoutOrNull` block.
## Other Improvements Made
1. **Changed Dispatcher to IO**: - Before: `CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main + SupervisorJob())` - After: `CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.IO + SupervisorJob() + exceptionHandler)` - `Dispatchers.IO` is better for Bluetooth scanning (blocking operations)
2. **Added CoroutineExceptionHandler**: ```kotlin private val exceptionHandler = CoroutineExceptionHandler { _, throwable -> android.util.Log.e("BluetoothHandler", "Uncaught coroutine exception: ${throwable.message}", throwable) } ``` - This catches any uncaught exceptions in coroutines - Previously, exceptions were being silently swallowed
3. **Enhanced Error Handling**: - Added try-catch around `scope.launch { }` to catch launch failures - Added thread name logging: `"startScanning coroutine started on thread: ${Thread.currentThread().name}"` - This helps debug which thread the coroutine runs on
## What You Must Do Now
### 1. Rebuild the App (CRITICAL!) The code on your phone is still the **broken version**. You MUST rebuild:
```powershell # In Android Studio: Build → Clean Project Build → Rebuild Project Run → Run 'app' ```
### 2. Test the Scan After installing the new version: 1. Open the app 2. Navigate to Bluetooth scan screen 3. Click "Scan for devices"
### 3. Check Logcat ```powershell adb logcat -c adb logcat | findstr "BluetoothHandler BluetoothRepo" ```
## Expected Logs After Fix
You should now see:
``` BluetoothHandler: startScan invoked from Flutter: duration=10000 BluetoothHandler: startScan pre-check missing permissions: [] BluetoothHandler: Checking if Bluetooth is enabled... BluetoothHandler: Bluetooth is enabled, checking location... BluetoothHandler: Location is enabled, calling startScanning... BluetoothHandler: startScanning called, launching coroutine with duration=10000 BluetoothHandler: Returning success to Flutter immediately BluetoothHandler: startScanning coroutine started on thread: DefaultDispatcher-worker-1 ← NEW! BluetoothHandler: About to call repository.startScan and collect flow ← NEW! BluetoothHandler: Inside withTimeoutOrNull, calling repository.startScan ← NEW! BluetoothRepo: startScan called with duration=10000ms ← NEW! BluetoothRepo: All pre-checks passed. Starting BLE scan... ← NEW! BluetoothRepo: BLE scan started successfully ← NEW! BluetoothRepo: Device found: name=..., address=... ← NEW! BluetoothHandler: Flow emitted X devices ← NEW! BluetoothHandler: Invoking onDevicesFound with X devices ← NEW! ```
## Why This Was Hard to Find
1. **Silent Failure**: The indentation error didn't cause a compilation error 2. **Coroutine Context**: Exceptions in coroutines can be silently swallowed without proper handlers 3. **No Exception Handler**: There was no `CoroutineExceptionHandler` to catch the error 4. **Return Immediately**: The code returned `result.success(null)` before the coroutine could fail
## Summary
- **Problem**: Indentation bug caused `repository.startScan()` to be outside the `withTimeoutOrNull` block - **Fix**: Corrected indentation + added exception handler + changed to IO dispatcher - **Next Step**: **REBUILD THE APP** and test again
The scan should now work properly!

# CRITICAL FIX APPLIED - Bluetooth Scanning Issue
## Problem Identified
From your logs at `21:38:05`: ``` BluetoothHandler: Location is enabled, calling startScanning... BluetoothHandler: startScanning called, launching coroutine with duration=10000 BluetoothHandler: Returning success to Flutter immediately ```
**Then NOTHING! No more logs from the coroutine.**
This means the coroutine was launching but **dying silently** without executing any code.
## Root Cause
The `CoroutineScope` was configured with `Dispatchers.Main`, but there was **no exception handler** to catch silent failures. When a coroutine throws an exception in the background, it can be silently swallowed unless you have a `CoroutineExceptionHandler`.
## Fixes Applied
### 1. Changed Dispatcher to IO ```kotlin // BEFORE: private val scope = CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main + SupervisorJob())
// AFTER: private val exceptionHandler = CoroutineExceptionHandler { _, throwable -> android.util.Log.e("BluetoothHandler", "Uncaught coroutine exception: ${throwable.message}", throwable) } private val scope = CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.IO + SupervisorJob() + exceptionHandler) ```
**Why**: - `Dispatchers.IO` is better for blocking operations like Bluetooth scanning - `CoroutineExceptionHandler` will catch and log ANY exception that occurs in the coroutine - This will reveal what's killing the coroutine
### 2. Added Comprehensive Exception Handling
Added multiple layers of try-catch: 1. **Outer try-catch** around the entire `scope.launch { }` block 2. **Inner try-catch** inside the coroutine 3. **Exception handler** in the CoroutineScope itself
### 3. Enhanced Logging
Added logging to track thread execution: ```kotlin android.util.Log.d("BluetoothHandler", "startScanning coroutine started on thread: ${Thread.currentThread().name}") ```
## What to Do Now
### 1. Rebuild and Install ```powershell # In Android Studio: Build → Clean Project → Build → Rebuild Project → Run ```
### 2. Test Again - Open app - Navigate to Bluetooth scan screen - Start scan
### 3. Check Logs ```powershell adb logcat | findstr "BluetoothHandler BluetoothRepo" ```

Based on the silent failure, the most likely causes are:
1. **Security Exception** - Missing a permission check somewhere 2. **Context Issue** - The `context` object is invalid when the coroutine runs 3. **Flow Collection Issue** - The Flow from `repository.startScan()` throws immediately

### Option 2: ADB Command Line ```bash adb logcat | findstr "BluetoothRepo WifiRepository BluetoothHandler WifiHandler" ```

BluetoothRepo: BLE scan started successfully BluetoothRepo: Device found: name=MyDevice, address=XX:XX:XX:XX:XX:XX, rssi=-45 BluetoothRepo: Device found: name=AnotherDevice, address=YY:YY:YY:YY:YY:YY, rssi=-67 BluetoothRepo: Scan duration 10000ms completed. ## Common Error Patterns
### Error: "Location services are disabled" **Problem**: Location is OFF in device settings **Solution**: Settings → Location → Turn ON
### Error: "Missing permissions: [ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION]" **Problem**: User denied location permission **Solution**: Settings → Apps → Your App → Permissions → Grant Location
### Error: "Scan failed: Internal error" **Problem**: Usually means Location is disabled or permission issue **Solution**: Enable Location and grant all permissions
### No errors, but no devices found **Problem**: 1. No nearby devices broadcasting 2. Scan completed before any devices responded 3. Location disabled (fails silently on some Android versions)
**Solution**: 1. Ensure other Bluetooth/WiFi devices are nearby and active 2. Increase scan duration (currently 10 seconds) 3. Double-check Location is enabled

1. **Capture full logcat** and look for errors: ```bash adb logcat > debug_log.txt ```
2. **Check Android version compatibility**: - Android 12+ has stricter BLE permissions - Some devices don't support BLE properly
3. **Test on another device** if possible

**Cause:** TokenManager.getUserEmail() is returning null

### Issue 3: FlutterDashboardActivity Never Opens
**Cause:** Intent issue or Activity not registered
**Solution:** Verify AndroidManifest.xml has: ```xml <activity android:name=".ui.FlutterDashboardActivity" android:exported="false" android:theme="@style/LaunchTheme" ... /> ```
### Issue 4: "No user session found" in Flutter
**Cause:** ChannelManager.setUserSession() was not called

``` ✓ Step 1: Does login succeed? └─ Check for: "Success state reached!"
✓ Step 2: Is TokenManager called? └─ Check for: "Collected - Email: ..."

✓ Step 7: Is session stored? └─ Check for: "User session stored in ChannelManager"
✓ Step 8: Is Flutter calling MethodChannel? └─ Check for: "MethodChannel call: getUserSession"

## Emergency Debug: Add Even More Logging
**In LoginFragment.navigateToFlutterDashboard():**
```kotlin android.util.Log.d("LoginFragment-START", "navigateToFlutterDashboard START")
CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main).launch { android.util.Log.d("LoginFragment-COROUTINE", "In Main coroutine")

# Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) Integration
This document explains how FCM notifications are implemented in the Android app.
## Features Implemented
1. **FCM Service** - `MyFirebaseMessagingService.kt` - Handles incoming push notifications - Manages FCM token refresh - Supports both notification and data payloads - Custom handling for different notification types (payment, promotion, etc.)
2. **Notification Channels** - `NotificationHelper.kt` - General notifications - Payment notifications (high priority) - Promotion notifications (low priority)
3. **Permission Handling** - `PermissionHelper.kt` - Handles Android 13+ notification permission requests - Automatically requests permission on app launch
4. **FCM Token Management** - Token is automatically fetched and saved to SharedPreferences - Token is refreshed when needed - Subscribe to "all_users" topic by default
## How to Test FCM
### 1. Get Your FCM Token
When you run the app, the FCM token will be logged in Logcat. Look for: ``` FCM Token: [your-token-here] ```
You can also retrieve it programmatically: ```kotlin val token = (application as AuthApplication).getFCMToken() ```
### 2. Send Test Notification from Firebase Console
1. Go to Firebase Console: https://console.firebase.google.com/ 2. Select your project 3. Go to **Cloud Messaging** in the left menu 4. Click **Send your first message** or **New campaign** 5. Enter notification details: - **Notification title**: Test Notification - **Notification text**: This is a test message 6. Click **Send test message** 7. Paste your FCM token 8. Click **Test**
### 3. Send Notification using Firebase Cloud Messaging API
You can send notifications from your backend server using the Firebase Cloud Messaging API:
```bash curl -X POST https://fcm.googleapis.com/fcm/send \ -H "Authorization: key=YOUR_SERVER_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "to": "DEVICE_FCM_TOKEN", "notification": { "title": "Payment Successful", "body": "Your payment of $50 has been processed" }, "data": { "type": "payment_status", "amount": "50", "transaction_id": "TXN123456" } }' ```
### 4. Send Notification to Topic
Send to all users subscribed to "all_users" topic:
```bash curl -X POST https://fcm.googleapis.com/fcm/send \ -H "Authorization: key=YOUR_SERVER_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "to": "/topics/all_users", "notification": { "title": "New Promotion", "body": "Get 20% off on your next purchase" } }' ```
## Notification Types
The app supports different notification types that can be handled differently:
1. **Payment Status** (`type: "payment_status"`) 2. **Promotion** (`type: "promotion"`) 3. **General** (default)
You can add more types in `MyFirebaseMessagingService.kt`:
```kotlin when (type) { "payment_status" -> { // Handle payment notification sendNotification(title, body) } "promotion" -> { // Handle promotion notification sendNotification(title, body) } "new_message" -> { // Handle new message notification sendNotification(title, body) } else -> { sendNotification(title, body) } } ```
## Sending Token to Backend
To send the FCM token to your backend server, update the `sendRegistrationToServer()` method in `MyFirebaseMessagingService.kt`:
```kotlin private fun sendRegistrationToServer(token: String) { // Example: Send to your backend lifecycleScope.launch { try { val response = apiService.updateFCMToken(token) if (response.isSuccessful) { Timber.d("Token sent to server successfully") } } catch (e: Exception) { Timber.e(e, "Failed to send token to server") } } } ```
## Notification Payload Examples
### Simple Notification ```json { "to": "DEVICE_TOKEN", "notification": { "title": "Hello", "body": "World" } } ```
### Notification with Data ```json { "to": "DEVICE_TOKEN", "notification": { "title": "Payment Received", "body": "You received $100" }, "data": { "type": "payment_status", "amount": "100", "sender": "John Doe" } } ```
### Data Only (Silent Notification) ```json { "to": "DEVICE_TOKEN", "data": { "type": "sync_data", "action": "refresh" } } ```
## Important Notes
1. **Android 13+**: Users must grant notification permission 2. **Background Restrictions**: Notifications may not work if the app is force-stopped 3. **Token Refresh**: FCM tokens can change, so always listen for token updates 4. **Server Key**: Keep your Firebase Server Key secure and never expose it in client code
## Troubleshooting
### Notifications not showing?
1. Check if notification permission is granted (Android 13+) 2. Verify FCM token is being generated (check Logcat) 3. Make sure google-services.json is properly added 4. Check if the app is in foreground or background 5. Verify Firebase project configuration
### Token not generated?
1. Ensure google-services.json is in the correct location 2. Check if Google Play Services is installed on the device 3. Verify internet connection 4. Check Logcat for errors
## Analytics Integration
FCM is integrated with Firebase Analytics. You can track: - Notification received events - Notification clicked events - User engagement with notifications
All notification interactions are automatically tracked in Firebase Analytics.

### 2. FlutterDashboardActivity.kt - UPDATED ```kotlin // Use cached Flutter engine from MainActivity override fun getCachedEngineId(): String { return "main" // Same ID as cached in MainActivity } ```
Now both activities share the SAME FlutterEngine instance!
---
## Complete Fixed Flow
``` MainActivity.onCreate() ├─ Create FlutterEngine ├─ Start Dart execution ├─ Setup ChannelManager (with THIS engine) ├─ Cache engine: FlutterEngineCache.put("main", flutterEngine) └─ Show login UI
LoginFragment └─ User logs in → navigateToFlutterDashboard()
FlutterDashboardActivity.onCreate() ├─ Extract intent extras (email, userId, token) ├─ Store in ChannelManager ├─ getCachedEngineId() returns "main" └─ Reuses MainActivity's cached FlutterEngine!
MethodChannel Communication ├─ FlutterDashboardActivity configures MethodChannel ├─ Uses SHARED FlutterEngine └─ Flutter dashboard can now communicate! ```

### ✅ FlutterDashboardActivity.kt ```kotlin // Added: private val ENGINE_ID = "main" override fun getCachedEngineId(): String { return ENGINE_ID } ```
